name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,778

entries.clue: Broken cab that the PM and I want to get going (5,2,3,3)

indicators.note: a broken thing is in pieces, ready to be put back together another way

annotation.surface: A prime minister and a companion stuck in a broken-down taxi, itching to be on their way.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'and' simply adds I to the rest of the fodder. The surface even fits the answer: stranded passengers really would champ at the bit.
annotation.definitionFit: A horse champing at the bit is impatient to start, so the phrase means to want to get going.

entries.clue: In the evening, one that's pulled short adult gets hot (7)

definitions.text: In the evening, one that's pulled

blocks.note: in = hot, fashionable; 'gets' just attaches it

annotation.surface: Someone out in the evening pulls a short adult who then gets hot under the collar.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pulled' in the surface suggests picking someone up on a night out; in the definition it is drawing a curtain at dusk.
annotation.definitionFit: Curtains are the thing you pull closed in the evening.

entries.clue: A trimmed physique emaciated leader digs (5)

indicators.note: a trimmed word has its end cut off
the leader of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: BODY, a physique, loses its last letter

annotation.surface: A slimmed-down, skeletal team leader is out digging.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Digs' looks like a verb at the end of the sentence, but it is the British noun for lodgings, a rented room.
annotation.definitionFit: Digs is informal British for lodgings, a place you live: an abode.

entries.clue: Jam infused with drop of rum is a sensation (7)

indicators.note: something infused with a flavour has it put inside
a drop is a tiny first taste, the first letter

blocks.note: a jam = a pickle, a tight spot
first letter of rum, placed inside PICKLE after the P

annotation.surface: Jam laced with rum makes a sensational spread.
annotation.walkthrough: Jam is not the fruit preserve but a predicament, which is also what a pickle is.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the tingling you feel on your skin is a physical sensation.

entries.clue: One stepping on European tackled by person on pitch? (7)

indicators.note: one player tackled by another is wrapped up in the tackle

blocks.note: a market trader works from a pitch, a stall site
E = European, placed inside TRADER after TR

annotation.surface: A footballer gets stood on by a European and is tackled on the pitch.
annotation.walkthrough: The pitch is not a football field but the spot where a street or market trader sets up.
annotation.definitionFit: A treader is one who treads, that is, steps on something.

entries.clue: Hard group detaining American guy with trouble in Bow? (7)

indicators.note: to detain is to hold inside

blocks.note: US = American, held between H and BAND

annotation.surface: A tough gang holds an American man who has got into trouble in Bow.
annotation.walkthrough: Bow is in London's East End, home of Cockney rhyming slang, where 'trouble and strife' means wife. A guy with a wife is a husband.
annotation.definitionFit: In Cockney slang 'trouble' is a wife, so a man with one is a husband.

entries.clue: Bleep hams out for utter profanities (9)

indicators.note: letters that are out are out of place

annotation.surface: A censor bleeping out swearing actors on air.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface fits the answer neatly: the bleep is what covers profanities on television.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: speaking irreverently of sacred things means uttering profanities.

entries.clue: Touch of tumultuous flatus engulfs knight and earl combined (7)

indicators.note: a touch is the smallest bit, the first letter
to engulf is to swallow up inside

blocks.note: N = knight in chess notation, E = earl; they go inside WIND after WIN

annotation.surface: A noble pair are overcome by a thunderous bout of flatulence.
annotation.walkthrough: Knight is N, not K, because K is already the king in chess notation.
annotation.definitionFit: Twinned means paired or joined, that is, combined.

entries.clue: What might affect drunk member I sponsored to get smashed? (10)

indicators.note: smashed things are broken up, here the letters

annotation.surface: A club member I sponsored went out and got drunk.
annotation.walkthrough: Smashed doubles as slang for drunk. The 'member' is not a club member but the body part that drooping afflicts after too much drink.
annotation.definitionFit: Heavy drinking can leave a man's member droopy, so droopiness is what might affect it.

entries.clue: Callas possibly missing intro in this? (4)

definitions.text: Callas possibly missing intro in this?

indicators.note: a word missing its intro has lost its first letter

blocks.note: Maria Callas, the opera singer; 'possibly' because other Marias exist

annotation.surface: Opera diva Maria Callas fluffs the opening of a solo.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: the wordplay makes ARIA, and 'in this' points to the solo song a soprano like Callas would sing.
annotation.definitionFit: An aria is an operatic solo, the kind of piece Callas was famous for.

entries.clue: Dissolute chap and a king arrested by soldiers (4)

indicators.note: someone arrested is held, here inside another word

blocks.note: A as printed plus K = king, placed inside RE

annotation.surface: A debauched man and a monarch are taken into custody by troops.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface places the chap and the king side by side, but only the king (with A) is arrested; the chap is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A rake is a dissolute, pleasure-seeking man.

entries.clue: Young person being dozy can cause offence (10)

blocks.note: a kid is a young person

annotation.surface: A sleepy teenager manages to offend people.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Offence' reads as hurt feelings; it is a crime, and a kid napping is literally kid-napping.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: seizing and holding a person is a crime, and offence is the legal word for one.

entries.clue: A Parisian that's fit, but impotent? (6)

annotation.surface: A fit-looking Frenchman who nevertheless cannot perform.
annotation.walkthrough: The joke is that ABLE sits inside UNABLE: the fit man is not able after all.
annotation.definitionFit: Impotent means powerless, unable to act.

entries.clue: A Dove product perhaps for an unmanageable hair do? (5-4)

blocks.note: a dove, like any bird, produces a nest
a tangled mess of hair is likened to what a bird builds

annotation.surface: An advert for a Dove shampoo that tames unruly hair.
annotation.walkthrough: Dove is a toiletries brand, and the capital D pushes you towards it; here it is simply the bird, whose product is its nest.
annotation.definitionFit: A dove builds a bird's nest, and messy, tangled hair is called a bird's-nest.

entries.clue: You could say the Cuban leader's a ginger (7)

blocks.note: Cuba is communist, and red is the colour of communism

annotation.surface: Fidel Castro was, loosely speaking, a ginger.
annotation.walkthrough: 'You could say' excuses the loose logic: a communist leader is a red head. Ginger is British slang for someone with red hair.
annotation.definitionFit: A ginger is a person with red hair, a redhead.

entries.clue: Warning: old man heading for wife is bit of a dog (7)

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: A warning that the old man on his way to meet his wife is a bit of a dog.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bit of a dog' reads as an insult about the old man; it is literally a part of a dog.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by part: a dog's front foot is literally one bit of the dog.

entries.clue: Damned short bird that often appears half-legless? (7)

indicators.note: a word cut short loses its last letter

blocks.note: flamingos famously stand on one leg

annotation.surface: A cursed, drunken creature, half legless.
annotation.walkthrough: Legless is British slang for very drunk, which the surface leans on; the bird is literally on one leg of two.
annotation.definitionFit: Flaming is a mild British expletive, used like damned: 'that flaming car'.

entries.clue: Egyptian royal okay with series being broadcast (7)

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard, not seen

blocks.note: fair = okay, a row = a series

annotation.surface: A TV series about an Egyptian king gets an okay review.
annotation.walkthrough: In a British accent FAIR ROW and PHARAOH sound alike, since the R of fair is silent.
annotation.definitionFit: A pharaoh was a king of ancient Egypt.

entries.clue: Excerpt of new hit lampooning old Aussie leader (7)

indicators.note: an excerpt is a piece taken from within a text

annotation.surface: A clip from a new satirical hit mocking a former Australian prime minister.
annotation.walkthrough: Gough Whitlam was Australian prime minister in the 1970s, and was indeed much lampooned.
annotation.definitionFit: Gough Whitlam led Australia as prime minister from 1972 to 1975.

entries.clue: Nipple ring (6)

blocks.note: the surface makes this the site of a piercing; the setter means the part of the body itself
not jewellery but a natural circle of darker skin surrounding it

annotation.surface: A piece of body-piercing jewellery.
annotation.walkthrough: The phrase suggests a piercing; read literally it is the natural ring surrounding the nipple.
annotation.definitionFit: The areola is the circular ring of pigmented skin around the nipple.

entries.clue: Tip from left-wing boards incenses line managers (7)

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter
to board is to get on inside, taking a passenger in

blocks.note: first letter of left-wing, placed inside ANGERS after ANG

annotation.surface: A left-wing activist boarding a bus infuriates middle management.
annotation.walkthrough: Line managers are office bosses in the surface; here they are people managing fishing lines.
annotation.definitionFit: Anglers handle fishing lines, so they are managers of lines.

entries.clue: I learnt about a place men go in the military (7)

definitions.text: a place men go in the military

indicators.note: letters moved about are rearranged

annotation.surface: A recruit recounts what he learned about army life.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'concerning'; it is the instruction to rearrange I LEARNT.
annotation.definitionFit: A latrine is a camp toilet, where soldiers go.

entries.clue: Having downed last of grappa, using neat rum is thus! (10)

definitions.text: Having downed last of grappa, using neat rum is thus!

indicators.note: to down a drink is to take it in, adding it to the mix
the last of a word is its final letter
rum means odd, strange, so the letters come out strangely

annotation.surface: Downing grappa and then drinking rum straight turns the stomach.
annotation.walkthrough: Rum looks like the drink but is the old adjective for odd. The whole clue is also the definition: mixing spirits neat like this is nauseating.
annotation.definitionFit: Knocking back grappa and neat rum would make anyone feel sick, which is what nauseating means.

entries.clue: I oppose all narrow-mindedness, Trumpism and idiots primarily (4)

definitions.text: I oppose all narrow-mindedness, Trumpism and idiots primarily

indicators.note: primarily means firstly, so take the first letters

blocks.note: first letters of All Narrow-mindedness Trumpism Idiots

annotation.surface: A declaration of opposition to bigotry, Trump and fools.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: someone saying 'I oppose' all those things is anti them. Note 'and' is skipped.
annotation.definitionFit: Anti means opposed, which is what the speaker declares.

entries.clue: Vessel old drinker's club will grab over empty tumbler on counter (5)

indicators.note: to grab is to take hold of, holding inside
an emptied word keeps only its outer letters
counter means against the direction, so back to front

blocks.note: Alcoholics Anonymous, a club for former drinkers
TUMBLER emptied to TR, then reversed; O and RT go inside AA

annotation.surface: A pub regular grabs a glass off the bar to drain it.
annotation.walkthrough: Vessel suggests a drinking container, fitting the tumbler and bar; it is a blood vessel. Counter is not the bar but a reversal instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: The aorta is the main artery, a blood vessel.

entries.clue: Equipment given to European, a highly-strung sort beset by wind? (4)

definitions.text: a highly-strung sort beset by wind?

annotation.surface: A nervy, windy European is handed some gear.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Highly-strung' and 'beset by wind' sound like a nervous, flatulent person; a kite is literally on a high string and blown by the wind.
annotation.definitionFit: A kite flies high on a string and is buffeted by the wind.

entries.clue: Modify shower, putting in second of planks of a 4x4 type? (3-7)

indicators.note: put in means placed inside
the second letter of the word

blocks.note: second letter of planks, placed inside ALTER after AL

annotation.surface: Renovating a bathroom shower by fitting planks from a four-wheel-drive.
annotation.walkthrough: Shower is weather here, not a bathroom fitting.
annotation.definitionFit: A 4x4 is an all-terrain vehicle, built to go off-road.

entries.clue: These eggs must be cooked with meat, understand? (3,3,7)

indicators.note: cooked ingredients are altered, and to cook something can mean to fiddle it

annotation.surface: A cook insists the eggs go in the pan with the meat, and asks if that is clear.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface ends by asking 'understand?', which is the definition sitting in plain sight.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: receiving a message means grasping its point, so the phrase is everyday slang for understanding.
